# Riemann Hypothesis / Weil Positivity — Roadmap

*Generated by pm-riemann on 2026-08-13 09:20. Manual edits will be overwritten on next sweep
— push back via OVERRIDE mail or by editing the PM config.*

**Where this stands, in one paragraph.** `paper/positivity-obstruction.tex` contains an
**unconditional** upper bound, $\limsup\mu^{-1}\log s(\mu)\le-4\pi$, a rate Connes–Consani
plot as a figure and never name. Four supporting theorems were proved on 2026-08-12 (Q1, Q2,
Q3, H0), the numerics have a second independent implementation, the elementary layer is
machine-checked in Lean, the one external dependency has been tested, and the citation audit
is closed. **And the paper's thesis is unchanged by all of it:** the house-rule table gained
five rows for the five new theorems and *every one is sign-blind*. The prolate mechanism
governs magnitude; the sign is RH; the two do not connect, and that is the result. The open
question is no longer mathematical throughput — it is **who outside this fleet will read it**,
and Daniel has chosen the route (below).

## Gaps I'm watching

- **Lean covers the elementary layer only** — no Prop 4.2, no Theorem 5.2, nothing of Q2, Q3,
  H0, or the assembly. The top of the chain rests on prose proofs that one agent wrote and
  another read. mg-7fc6 is the first attempt to move this line; it may report that it cannot
  be moved without the mathlib build.
- **Still nobody outside this fleet has read a line.** Daniel has ruled that a human reviewer
  is the wrong instrument and Lean is the substitute; that is a real answer, and it is not the
  same thing as the risk being gone. The endorsement requirement partially re-imports it: an
  endorser must read enough to vouch.
- **No CI.** Fifteen `verify_*.py` scripts and a Lean check script, and nothing re-runs any of
  them. Reproducibility is currently a claim, not a mechanism.
- The vision document is past 1,000 lines. Its CURRENT STATE header is the only part a new
  reader should trust to be current.
